decision.next_allowed_work: Do not write a graph/dataflow runtime patch from current evidence. The remaining plausible classes are external verifier/speculative decoding with high acceptance, or a representation/model route with correctness/top1 proof. If those are unavailable, record that generalized >5 needs a new dataflow interface rather than local stream/cache tuning.
required_reopen_proof: A source/dataflow probe showing graph_gate_output_input_available > 0 or equivalent retained CUDA gate/topk/weights path in accepted graph.
A joint bound showing gate source + up/down movement are removed/hidden enough for all calibration prompts to exceed 5 tok/s with overhead margin.
Fixed-text top1/correctness proof before any strict cold candidate run.
16GB cgroup and 32GB VRAM accounting including gate cache/page cache/workspace.
decision.summary: Current DeepSeek4 graph/dataflow cannot be reopened for generalized >5 as-is. The graph still does not expose a retained gate output to build_expert_mix; DS4_HOT recomputes gate and carries extra hot tensor payload. Since up/down-only removal is not enough for generalized 5, this missing retained-gate/source-reuse interface is a hard blocker, not an implementation detail.

residual_decision.next_allowed_work: Run no source edits until a joint hard-bound exists. Evaluate exact graph/dataflow routes for retaining gate results and computing up/down without repeated source movement, or a representation route with top1/correctness proof. If neither has a hard bound above generalized 5 with overhead margin, record the blocker.
residual_decision.reason: A runtime patch that only moves up/down fallback to a new exact path is unlikely to produce stable generalized >5 tok/s. The next candidate must remove or hide both up/down and gate/source/residual costs, or reduce model/representation payload while preserving correctness.
residual_decision.summary: Generalized 5 tok/s requires more than a narrow up/down fallback implementation. Ideal decode up/down removal leaves quantum/fibonacci below target under the stricter 40-layer bound and leaves fibonacci below target even under 43-layer sensitivity. Gate source/cache time is a same-order bottleneck in trace data.

old_graph_bound_reused_facts.reason: The current exact graph/dataflow candidates all fail a hard gate: current DS4 graph has no retained gate output, current DS4_HOT recomputes gate and inflates payload, sparse retained top64 has only 18.947 ms theoretical margin and no dataflow proof, exact hot/full kernels are 3-5x too slow for the relevant bounds, and full payload/layer placement violates VRAM or gate-cache tradeoffs.
reopen_conditions: A placement probe must show a real retained CUDA gate/up/down path in the accepted DeepSeek4 graph: graph_gate_output_input_available > 0, hot_active/hot_ready > 0, and hidden scheduler copies counted.

A compact sparse branch must prove final combine/scheduler/launch/sync overhead with meaningful margin above the 18.947 ms paper bound; a one-copy lower bound that leaves only 1.75 ms margin is not enough.

An exact kernel route must demonstrate fixed-text top1 and measured effective bandwidth above the relevant threshold, e.g. >246 GiB/s for top128 before integration overhead, with H2D/D2H/scatter/sync included.
A full-MoE route must provide a new payload/VRAM/RAM proof; current 21.806 GiB unique up/down payload and 16GB page-cache limit reject full residency.
Any reopened source probe must be default-off, pass fixed-text top1 under strict 16GB/no-swap cgroup, preserve the default accepted path, and only then proceed to strict cold France benchmarking.
